function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to directly measure your connection from here, but you can quickly check your internet speed yourself. Here are a few easy options: | Method | How to use it | What you’ll see | |--------|---------------|-----------------| | **Web browser** | Go to (or ) and click “Go” or “Start.” | Download speed, upload speed, and ping. | | **Command line (Windows)** | Open PowerShell or Command Prompt and run:
`powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py -OutFile speedtest.py; python speedtest.py --simple"` | A quick text output of download/upload speeds. | | **Command line (Linux/macOS)** | Open Terminal and run:
`curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py > speedtest.py && python3 speedtest.py --simple` | Same as above. | | **Speedtest‑CLI (Python package)** | If you have Python installed, run:
`pip install speedtest-cli`
`speedtest-cli --simple` | Text output of speeds. | ### Quick command‑line test (if you have Python) If you’re comfortable running a command, you can use the `speedtest-cli` Python package. Here’s a one‑liner that downloads the script, runs it, and prints the results: ```bash curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py > speedtest.py && python3 speedtest.py --simple ``` If you’re on Windows and prefer PowerShell: ```powershell powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py -OutFile speedtest.py; python speedtest.py --simple" ``` ### What the numbers mean - **Download speed** – How fast data comes *to* you (measured in Mbps). - **Upload speed** – How fast data goes *from* you (also Mbps). - **Ping** – Latency, measured in milliseconds (ms). Lower is better for gaming, video calls, etc. If you’d like me to run a command on your machine (e.g., the PowerShell snippet above), just let me know and I’ll execute it for you. Otherwise, try one of the methods above and let me know what you get!
